content:
Maria L.: quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a small inbound "converter shim" that translates legacy multipart/envelope requests into the new JSON-envelope shape at our edge. goal is to avoid breaking older clients while we finish the migration.
Sam P.: need a design sketch. is this a sidecar, gateway module, or an infra shim?
Maria L.: gateway module (nginxlua plugin on the ingress tier) that does minimal parsing and emits the normalized body to the service. keeps auth & routing intact.
Kevin R.: +1 for minimalism. two main concerns: latency and explosion of code paths (testing burden). how much per-request overhead?
Maria L.: measured a naïve PoC: ~1.8ms median overhead on p50 for small payloads, and ~6-8ms p95 for large 2MB multipart bodies. still way under our 100ms SLO for these endpoints, but affects tail.
Tanya (SRE): do we have a clear rollback plan? if the shim causes CPU spikes under load we need fast kill switch and circuit-breaker.
Maria L.: plan: feature-flagged rollout behind tenant opt-in. defaults off. canary on 5 tenants, monitor cpu, request latency, error-rate, and request size histograms. also expose shim-specific metric `shim.converter.rejected_malformed` and `shim.converter.latency_ms`.
Sam P.: will this touch auth headers or X-forwarded stuff? we need to keep traces intact (traceparent).
Maria L.: preserves all headers; we only mutate body and add `X-Redwood-Shim: converter-v1` for telemetry.
Kevin R.: what about caching and prefix-KV cache? converting shapes may prevent cache hits for existing routes.
Maria L.: good point. shim preserves canonical request fingerprint: if the client had an envelope form that maps to the same route+input, the shim will rewrite a synthetic deterministic canonical body so downstream cache keys stay stable. implemented as: `sha256(route||normalized_body)`.
Tanya (SRE): add a gauge of cache-hit-rates before/after for the canary tenants. also watch token-level cost metrics — doubling tokens unexpectedly kills budgets.
Sam P.: testing matrix? unit tests + integration + load. Also need e2e with older SDKs.
Maria L.: tests: parser fuzzing (+1000 random multipart cases), schema conformance, golden fixtures of historical payloads, and a small chaos test where shim is toggled on/off mid-request.
Kevin R.: any security concerns? multipart parsing historically had CVEs in some libs.
Maria L.: using sandboxed lua parser with strict size limits (default 8MB), rejects polymorphic content and logs to `shim.converter.rejected_malformed` with sample hash for triage. we will also run static fuzzer on parser for a week before canary.
Tanya (SRE): operational ops: make sure rollback is one API call to flip feature flag. also a kill-switch endpoint in ingress admin that disables converter globally and returns 503 with `Retry-After`.
Sam P.: what's the migration window? are we expecting clients to update?
Maria L.: recommended 90 days. plan: start canary, monitor, then opt-in beta (30 tenants) for 2 weeks, then incremental opt-in via percentage rollout over 2 weeks, then announce deprecation of envelope variant after 60 days of wide opt-in.
Kevin R.: telemetry quotas? telemetry will add labels and metrics. ensure cardinality stays low (no tenant-specific labels except for canary flag).
Maria L.: agreed. label only: `env` and `shim_version` and `status` (ok/error/rejected).
infra-bot: [automated] Created canary dashboard at https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/conv-shim/conv-shim-canary showing shim.latency_ms, shim.rejected_malformed, req.duration, host.cpu.
Tanya (SRE): add alert: `alert if shim.rejected_malformed > 1 for 5m` and `alert if shim.latency_p95 increases by >30% vs baseline`.
Maria L.: scheduled. I'll also add a `shim.emergency_disable` event to our runbook.
Sam P.: runtime perf: maybe we can JIT-compile some common envelope patterns to reduce tail overhead. but that is deferred — first iteration must be simplest.
Kevin R.: and document the behaviour in our API compatibility playbook: where shims live, telemetry expectations, rollback steps.
Maria L.: will draft the short RFC follow-up and add to `eng-infra` RFC folder. also hooking up a postmortem checklist if we see regressions.
Tanya (SRE): load test plan: run a 10k rps ramp against canary stack with synthetic multipart payloads and record p99, p995 for both canary and control. if p995 delta > 50ms, abort.
Maria L.: noted. I'll post the test script:
```
curl -X POST https://canary-ingress.redwood.test/api/v1/generate \
  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \
  -F "file=@big_payload.json" \
  --header "X-Tenant: t-canary" \
  --insecure
```
Sam P.: any DB schema changes?
Maria L.: none. shim is stateless at ingress.
Kevin R.: fallback semantics: if shim rejects malformed, we currently return 400. can we offer `accept-legacy-fallback=true` param to route to a slower compatibility worker?
Maria L.: we considered a slow-path worker but it complicates ops. prefer to fail fast and provide clear error to clients, with a temporary support flag for critical tenants.
Tanya (SRE): make sure support flag requires manual approval and audit log.
Maria L.: yup — support flag gated by a runbook and my sig-off.
deploy-bot: [staging] deploy started for `conv-shim:feature/ingress-normalizer` to canary cluster at 2026-03-17T12:34:00Z
Sam P.: thanks — please ping when metrics appear. :eyes:
Kevin R.: +1 to iterate quickly after canary results.
Maria L.: will schedule a 30-min check-in 24h after canary goes live to decide whether to expand. thanks all. :thumbsup:
